name: Conveyor Line A
notes: Main assembly line conveyor. Belt speed range: 10–60 FPM via VFD. Belt last replaced August 2023 — inspect monthly for edge fraying. Do not exceed 200 lb/ft distributed load.

parts.notes: Full belt replacement. Keep one roll in stock at all times.
Replace if noisy or rough when spun by hand.
Pillow block style. Grease fitting on top — grease every 90 days.
Parameter backup file stored on USB in electrical cabinet. Restore from backup if drive is replaced.

pins.description: VFD internal 24V supply output — use for digital inputs only
Digital input 2 — Stop command (normally closed circuit)
Digital input 3 — Fault clear (momentary pulse clears active fault)

troubleshooting.symptom: Belt tracks to one side and rides against the frame
steps: Stop the conveyor. Never try to adjust belt tracking while the belt is running under load.
Check that the head pulley and tail pulley are both square to the conveyor frame — use a tape measure to compare drive side and operator side measurements.
Inspect the take-up assembly. Unequal tension on left vs. right will cause the belt to walk toward the tighter side.
Adjust the take-up bearing on the side the belt is walking TOWARD — tighten that side slightly to push the belt back to center.
Make small adjustments (1/4 turn at a time) then jog the conveyor to observe the effect before further adjustment.
Check all carrier rollers for free spin — a seized roller will cause the belt to drag and track off.

troubleshooting.symptom: VFD displays Fault F12 (Overcurrent) and shuts down
steps: Clear the fault by momentarily energizing DI3 (Fault Clear input) or using the VFD keypad.
Check for any mechanical binding in the conveyor — rotate the belt by hand to confirm it moves freely.
Verify belt tension is not excessive — overtightened belt greatly increases motor load.
Check that the acceleration ramp time parameter (P053) is not set too short. A rapid acceleration ramp causes high inrush current. Increase ramp time to 3–5 seconds.
Check motor wiring connections at the VFD output terminals (T1, T2, T3) for looseness or corrosion.
If F12 persists at no-load, the VFD current limit may need adjustment or the motor may have a winding fault — measure motor winding resistance phase-to-phase (should be equal within 5%).
